gap: The caret is 8px wide with square-cut ends and sits 3px lower than A's (blue bar y=372–463 vs 369–460, i.e. ~30px below the line-3 baseline vs ~27px); A's is 9px with rounded caps and hangs less into the interline gap. That is a sub-pixel-class complaint next to A's marker problem, and it is the only thing B loses on.
gapTheirs: Syntax markers are undimmed: both asterisks around *never* measure #1c1c1c — pixel-identical to the body ink (#1c1c1c on #f9f9f9) — so they read as two black glyphs sitting in the sentence rather than as markup. B renders the same asterisks at #7a7a7a, roughly 2.5x lighter against the page, so the italic carries the emphasis and the syntax recedes. This is the one typographic decision that separates the two images, and A gets it backwards.
verdict: These two are the same page — same face, same 92px line pitch (~1.6 ratio), same #1c1c1c ink on #f9f9f9, same measure at 47 characters, same true cursive italic rather than a slanted roman — except for one thing, and it is the thing that decides whether markdown is bearable to write in. A prints the emphasis asterisks at full body weight, so the eye trips over them twice per emphasised word and the line's grey texture is punctured; B drops them to #7a7a7a and the sentence reads as prose while the italic still announces itself. A's caret is marginally better shaped (9px, rounded, 3px higher), which buys it nothing. Neither shows a blank line, so paragraph spacing is untested in both — fix that in the next sample.

builderNote: Re-measured iA's type by advance-fitting the Duo cell across four captures (REFERENCE.md's x-height ems are ~2% low): leading is liquid, pitch = 1.30 x size + 10.4px, now computed in --line-pitch and rounded to whole pixels once so page.css and caret.js read the same number the text is set on — that mismatch had been walking #mirror off #input 0.4px per line. Default size 18 -> 20px (iA's own window capture), measure 64ch, kerning/ligatures/calt off, per-theme optical weight (415 on paper, 400 on dark) which brings our measured ink per line to within 1% of iA on both themes. Swapped to the variable iA faces (two files per family; the upright covers bold, so bold no longer fetches a font mid-keystroke), warmed the italic cut at boot, and patched iA's Quattro Italic word space (600 -> 450 units, gvar frozen) back onto the grid — it was sliding every italic run a character out from under the caret. Hanging markers deliberately skipped: not metric-safe over a textarea.
secondary: Both images are 1930x700, same viewport, and diff to zero outside the *never* run and a 3px caret offset.

B's marker grey #7a7a7a on #f9f9f9 is only about 4:1 contrast — legible, but it is the ceiling of how far this approach can dim before the markers become unfindable when editing; consider dimming further only on unfocused lines.
Line pitch 92px against a cap height of roughly 39px gives about 1.6 leading in both — defensible for a 47-character measure, but neither image proves it holds across a paragraph break.

Caret is a full-line-box 92px bar in both, i.e. it spans ascender to descender rather than the type's own extent; A's rounded caps soften this slightly, B's square ends make the overshoot more obvious.
